items.title: Mines Ministry panel to rewrite the 2019 National Mineral Policy, naming recycling and critical minerals as priorities
items.summary: The Mines Ministry has formed a nine-member panel, chaired by an Additional Secretary, to review the National Mineral Policy, 2019 and recommend a comprehensive revision within two months, PTI reports citing sources. Recycling, critical minerals and deep-sea resources are named as the new priorities, alongside a planned recast of the MMDR Act, 1957.
items.why: If recycling gets a formal place in national mineral policy, it could shape future incentives and rules for India's e-waste and battery recyclers.

items.title: China's rare earth magnet exports hit a 2026 high of about 6,165 tonnes in September
items.summary: China exported 6,165 tonnes of rare earth permanent magnets in September, up 23% from August and 6.7% from a year earlier, the highest monthly figure this year, as backlogged orders were released, according to SMM. Exports for January to September totalled 48,055 tonnes, up 20% year on year.
items.why: SMM counts India among the markets driving demand, and steadier Chinese magnet supply sets the price bar that India's planned magnet plants and magnet recyclers must compete with.

items.title: Phoenix Tailings plans $375 million rare earth separation plant in New York that will also take recycled feed
items.summary: Phoenix Tailings will build a plant in Rochester, New York, to process more than 18,000 tons a year of mined and recycled rare earth feedstock into over 4,400 tons of separated oxides, ramping up in 2027 and reaching full capacity in 2028. It is part of a $1.2 billion project backed by a $500 million conditional loan commitment from the US Office of Strategic Capital.
items.why: Large Western separation capacity that accepts recycled feed creates more buyers for magnet scrap outside China, a market Indian magnet recyclers could target.

items.title: Öko-Institut study says recycling batteries in the EU could cut virgin cobalt demand by 60-70%
items.summary: An Öko-Institut study commissioned by members of the EU Raw Materials Coalition finds that recycling lithium-ion batteries inside the EU could reduce virgin demand by 25-50% for lithium, 60-70% for cobalt and 35-50% for nickel. It also says smaller EVs and lighter batteries could trim mineral needs by about 17% by 2035, and calls for specific recycling targets and more funding for recycling plants.
items.why: It gives Indian policymakers and recyclers a benchmark for how much recycling can offset imported lithium, cobalt and nickel as India builds out its own critical-mineral recycling incentives.

items.title: Korea's recyclers struggle to make money from LFP batteries as their share of EVs grows
items.summary: LFP cells held over 65% of the global EV cathode market in January–August 2026, but their recoverable value rests mostly on lithium (about $9.59/kg last year) rather than cobalt ($34.21/kg) or nickel ($15.2/kg). Korea recovered 65.9% of mandatory-return EV batteries between 2021 and August 2026, and industry is asking for recycled-content mandates and clarity on who pays to treat low-value LFP packs.
items.why: India's EV and storage fleet is leaning heavily on LFP, so Indian recyclers and EPR planners face the same question of how to fund recycling of chemistries with little cobalt or nickel to sell.

items.title: China's black mass output fell about 15% in September as LFP supply tightened
items.summary: SMM estimates China produced roughly 56,000 tonnes of lithium battery black mass in September, about 15% less than in August, with LFP black mass driving most of the drop. Stricter rules on reusing old batteries, plant maintenance and sellers holding back scrap all cut volumes, while falling lithium carbonate and cobalt sulfate prices squeezed recycler margins.
items.why: Lower Chinese black mass output and thinner margins affect the payables and export demand Indian battery recyclers see for their own black mass.

items.title: POSCO's Korean recycling plant turns 12,000 tonnes of black mass a year into battery salts
items.summary: POSCO's battery recycling unit says its South Korean hydrometallurgy plant processes about 12,000 tonnes of black mass a year into 2,500 tonnes of lithium carbonate, 12,000 tonnes of nickel sulfate, 3,800 tonnes of cobalt sulfate and 2,000 tonnes of manganese sulfate. The plant reports recovering over 90% of the main valuable metals, and SNE Research expects used-battery volumes to grow from 44 GWh in 2025 to 3,339 GWh in 2040.
items.why: It is a benchmark for the scale and recovery rates Indian black mass refiners will need to compete with as they move beyond shredding.

items.title: Thailand plans dedicated industrial zones for recycling solar panels and EV batteries
items.summary: Thailand's Industry Ministry wants to group solar-panel and EV-battery recyclers with hazardous-waste facilities in controlled zones with shared wastewater treatment and round-the-clock monitoring, warning that panels installed about a decade ago could become significant waste within one to two years. It is also reviewing decades-old laws that cap dumping fines at 200,000 baht, with fines of up to tens of millions of baht and asset seizures under discussion.
items.why: India faces the same wave of first-generation solar panels and has no separate solar-waste rulebook yet, so Thailand's zone-plus-penalty model is a template Indian recyclers and regulators may be asked to match.

items.title: Ex-China rare earth prices hold steady as Lynas agrees A$968 million Meteoric deal
items.summary: SMM's ex-China weekly review put Pr-Nd oxide at $115-129/kg FOB and terbium oxide at $1,161-1,249/kg FOB, down $20/kg, with most other prices flat and trading thin. Lynas agreed to buy Meteoric Resources for about A$968 million to add Brazil's Caldeira ionic clay project, while Arafura raised its binding NdPr oxide offtake to 850 tonnes a year.
items.why: Ex-China oxide prices set the value of recovered Nd, Pr and Tb in magnet scrap, so Indian magnet recyclers and the new magnet-scheme bidders should track these benchmarks rather than Chinese domestic prices.

items.title: Jereh plans 85,000-tonne lithium battery recycling project in Jinan, China
items.summary: Jereh Resources Recycling Technology has opened environmental-impact review for a plant in Jinan, Shandong, with a 25,000 t/yr line for scrap LFP batteries and a 60,000 t/yr line for LFP and ternary batteries. The process runs from pack dismantling and crushing to oxygen-free pyrolysis and sorting, with black mass, copper and aluminium as outputs.
items.why: More Chinese pre-treatment capacity means more competition for global battery scrap and black mass, which can weigh on the prices Indian sellers are offered.

items.title: Malaysia discloses battery-waste volumes for the first time, but has no EV battery EPR yet
items.summary: A written parliamentary reply from Malaysia's environment ministry said 13,743 tonnes of SW103 battery waste were generated from 2021 to 2025, with seven licensed off-site recycling facilities operating as of March 2026. A mandatory EPR regime for EV battery recycling is still under study, and the Department of Environment is drafting amendments to blacklist repeat offenders.
items.why: India already runs battery EPR targets; neighbours without them remain loosely regulated sources of scrap, and a policy gap to watch for Indian recyclers sourcing in the region.

items.title: EU names cylib's Dormagen battery recycling plant a Strategic Project
items.summary: The European Commission picked German recycler cylib's project as a Strategic Project under the Critical Raw Materials Act; its hydrometallurgical plant in Dormagen, now under construction, is designed to handle up to 140,000 EV batteries a year. The label backs the Act's aim of meeting at least 25% of EU strategic raw material demand from recycling by 2030.
items.why: Europe is lining up permitting and finance support for domestic battery recycling, which will shape where black mass and recycled metals flow and the standard Indian recyclers selling into EU supply chains will be compared against.

items.title: Wayanad aims to be India's first e-waste-free district by 1 November
items.summary: Kerala's Wayanad district collected 31 tonnes of e-waste from government offices in the first phase of its drive (28–30 September), including 12 tonnes each from Kalpetta and Bathery and five from Mananthawady. The material goes to the state's Clean Kerala Company, and the district is targeting e-waste-free status by Keralam Formation Day on 1 November.
items.why: District drives that route institutional e-waste to a state agency show where formal recyclers can find steady volumes, and who they may be competing with for them.

items.title: China black mass payables slip after the National Day holiday as lithium and cobalt fall
items.summary: SMM put ternary electrode black mass payables at about 71–73% on 15 October, around 1.2 points below the first day after the holiday, while LFP electrode black mass fell 975 yuan per lithium percentage point to 4,800–5,300 yuan. Lithium carbonate was quoted at 101,800–107,000 yuan a tonne and cobalt sulphate is down more than 4,000 yuan a tonne since the break.
items.why: Chinese payables are a key reference for Indian black mass deals, so softer metal prices point to thinner margins for recyclers selling or buying this quarter.

items.title: Redwood Materials will now recycle Rivian's battery production scrap
items.summary: Rivian has widened its partnership with Redwood Materials, which will recycle scrap from Rivian's battery manufacturing on top of handling end-of-life packs. Redwood is also building a 10 MWh storage system at Rivian's Normal, Illinois plant from more than 100 second-life Rivian packs.
items.why: Production scrap is the cleanest, highest-value feedstock in battery recycling, and Indian recyclers chasing cell-maker scrap will face the same OEM-tied deals as gigafactories ramp up.

items.title: China's NdFeB scrap prices hold near highs as recyclers hesitate
items.summary: SMM's weekly review put recycled Pr-Nd at 755–765 yuan/kg, dysprosium at 1,230–1,250 yuan/kg and terbium at 5,600–5,800 yuan/kg, with Pr-Nd edging up mid-week alongside oxide prices. Recyclers were cautious about paying more, and SMM expects Pr-Nd scrap to consolidate at high levels.
items.why: Chinese scrap prices set the benchmark for what magnet swarf and end-of-life motors from India can fetch.

items.title: Chennai workshop calls for a separate rulebook for end-of-life solar panels
items.summary: Speakers at a Consumer and Civic Action Group workshop in Chennai said India needs a dedicated solar recycling policy, modelled on its e-waste rules. With a 280 GW solar target, they argued EPR alone has not delivered safe panel dismantling.
items.why: Solar panels sit inside the e-waste rules today. A separate framework would change who pays, and what recyclers can claim.

items.title: Ionic Rare Earths files plans for a commercial magnet recycling plant in Belfast
items.summary: Ionic Rare Earths submitted a planning application to Belfast City Council on 19 September for a commercial magnet recycling facility at Queen's Island. A decision is expected in Q1 2027, construction is planned from Q3 2027, and the company is working to secure a £12 million UK government capital grant.
items.why: Magnet-to-oxide recycling outside China is moving towards commercial scale, which is useful as a benchmark for Indian firms eyeing rare earth recovery from e-waste and motor scrap.

items.title: Fastmarkets restarts US black mass payables after export exemptions free up flows
items.summary: Fastmarkets resumed its ex-works US nickel and cobalt black mass payable assessments on 14 October. It had suspended them on 1 September, after a US Commerce Department rule banning black mass exports took effect on 27 August.
items.why: With the US price reference back, Indian buyers and refiners can again track US black mass against Asian payables. It also shows US export exemptions are letting some material move.

items.title: EU sold 14.6 million tonnes of electronics in 2024 but collected only 5.5 million tonnes of e-waste
items.summary: Citing Eurostat data for 2024, the European Environmental Bureau and other NGOs said electronics sales in the EU have risen 91% since 2012, while e-waste collection grew about 6% year on year to 5.5 million tonnes. Germany's collection rate was 28.7%, and preparing-for-reuse rates stay below 2%, as the groups push for tougher rules in the WEEE Directive revision.
items.why: A tighter EU WEEE regime will shape the compliance costs of global brands that also sell in India, and Europe's weak collection numbers are a reminder that EPR targets only work when collection is enforced.

items.title: N.A.N. Silox GreenMet breaks ground on ₹1,400 crore battery recycling plant in Andhra Pradesh
items.summary: The 50:50 venture between India's N.A.N. GreenMet and Belgium's Silox Group has secured Consent to Establish and started work on a lithium-ion battery recycling and critical-metals plant at Naidupeta. Capacity will be added in phases up to 40,000 tonnes a year of shredding and 20,000 tonnes a year of hydrometallurgical processing, making battery-grade salts; Vijay Pasupathy has been named CEO.
items.why: A domestic hydromet buyer of this size adds competition for Indian black mass and battery scrap, and moves the country closer to refining battery salts at home instead of shipping out intermediates.

items.title: Nexon Geochem plans ₹1,250 crore rare-earth magnet plant in Andhra Pradesh
items.summary: Hyderabad-based Nexon Geochem has signed an MoU with the Andhra Pradesh Economic Development Board for a sintered NdFeB magnet plant at Thondangi in Kakinada district, with ₹750 crore in phase one and ₹500 crore in phase two. The plant is designed to make 600 tonnes of permanent magnets a year for EVs, wind turbines, industrial automation and defence.
items.why: No dates were given, but a domestic sintered-magnet maker would give Indian rare-earth recyclers a potential local outlet for recovered NdPr and magnet scrap.

items.title: E-Waste Day 2026 targets cheap 'fast tech' like cables, earbuds and vapes
items.summary: A WEEE Forum study found that only 32% of low-cost gadgets were sent for recycling or reuse, while 39% of buyers had finished with them within a month. The UN estimates 62 million tonnes of e-scrap are generated each year, with only 22.3% recycled.
items.why: Small, low-value items are the hardest category to collect against EPR targets, and their embedded cells add to fire risk at recycling plants.

items.title: India reports 13.98 lakh tonnes of e-waste for 2024-25, but still doesn't count the informal workforce
items.summary: Published on International E-Waste Day, this piece notes the environment ministry's estimate of 13.98 lakh tonnes generated in 2024-25, with 70.7% reported as processed. It argues India tracks tonnes and certificates but not the informal workers who collect and dismantle most of it.
items.why: Collection targets rise to 80% from FY2027-28. The informal channel is where the missing tonnes are.

items.title: Singapore's NEU Battery Materials raises $7.6M and opens an LFP lithium recovery plant
items.summary: NEU closed a $7.6 million round co-led by Shift4Good and SGInnovate. It opened a plant in Tuas that can process about 1,300 tonnes a year of LFP scrap and black mass into battery-grade lithium. Europe and US expansion is planned from 2027.
items.why: LFP is the hard case for recyclers because it holds no nickel or cobalt. Lithium-only recovery economics will matter as India's LFP volumes grow.

items.title: Sri Lanka moves towards an EPR-based national e-waste system
items.summary: Sri Lanka's Environment Ministry is preparing amendments to the National Environmental Act and seeking approval for a national e-waste policy built around extended producer responsibility. Specific producer obligations have not yet been announced.
items.why: Another South Asian market adopting producer responsibility could open compliance and recycling work for Indian EPR service providers and recyclers next door.

items.title: New South Wales consults on Australia's first mandatory solar panel recycling scheme
items.summary: The NSW government has released a draft regulation and issues paper that would make solar panel brand owners pay for collecting and recycling end-of-life panels. The state has more than 1.18 million rooftop systems and about 14,000 tonnes of panel waste a year, expected to reach 89,000 tonnes by 2045.
items.why: It is a live example of solar-specific producer responsibility, which is the model Indian stakeholders are now asking for.

items.title: Ex-China terbium and dysprosium prices jump on US demand
items.summary: Fastmarkets' CIP global terbium oxide assessment rose to $5,000–8,000/kg, up 41% in a week. Dysprosium oxide moved to $2,500–3,500/kg. China's export controls keep these heavy rare earths scarce outside China.
items.why: Outside China, these magnet metals now sell at many times China's domestic price. That premium is what makes magnet recycling pay.

items.title: GM puts cathode made from recycled EV batteries into production vehicles
items.summary: With Cirba Solutions, GM turned 80 end-of-life EV packs into black mass and then more than 12 tonnes of new cathode material for Ultium Cells. The first cars built with it have come off the line in Michigan and Tennessee.
items.why: This is closed-loop proof at automaker scale. It is the benchmark Indian OEMs and recyclers will be measured against.

items.title: US lets ABTC export up to $100M of black mass despite export controls
items.summary: The US Commerce Department granted American Battery Technology Co. an exception to sell up to $100 million of recycled black mass abroad. US rules otherwise require black mass producers to sell their output domestically until August 2027.
items.why: US shredding capacity has run ahead of refining. Exceptions like this decide where black mass flows, and that affects payables in Asia.

items.title: Environment ministry's Special Campaign 6 targets 3,270 obsolete electronic items in its own offices
items.summary: MoEFCC's October 2–31 campaign includes an SOP for scientific disposal of office e-waste. It has flagged about 3,270 items across its offices, including 1,425 IT and telecom items.
items.why: Government offices are a steady source of e-waste. Campaign months are when authorised recyclers can win government lots.
